verdict.rationale: Asana's AI Teammates have a documented shared memory that carries forward feedback and preferences, so its in-app AI does learn user context over time. That memory is described at the team and workflow level, though, and nothing shows it learning an individual's writing tone or shorthand to tailor generated output. Missing for 10: explicit learning of personal tone and shorthand, per-user personalization controls, documentation of how learned preferences shape output, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have my in-app AI assistant learn my tone, shorthand, and preferences to tailor its output

citations.quote: Shared memory means AI Teammates learn from the work itself. Every completed task, every piece of feedback, every preference gets carried forward, so no one repeats context they've already given
Pre-built AI agents that work alongside your team inside real workflows, with shared memory, governance, and context from the Work Graph
